title: Performance and Power: Systematic Evaluation of AI Workloads on Accelerators with CARAML
problem: Evaluating ML workloads across diverse hardware accelerators from different vendors requires a systematic, reproducible framework that accurately measures both performance and energy consumption simultaneously.
motivation: As specialized ML accelerators proliferate from multiple vendors, understanding their relative performance and power efficiency is critical for informed deployment and architecture selection decisions.
method: CARAML is an automated benchmark suite that measures speed and power consumption of transformer-based large language models and computer vision models running on specialized hardware accelerators (chips optimized for AI) from different vendors. It uses a custom tool called jpwr to accurately measure power consumption. The design prioritizes compactness (minimal dependencies), extensibility (easy to add new tests or hardware), and reproducibility (consistent results across different systems).
key_novelty: CARAML automatically measures both speed and power consumption of AI workloads in a single unified framework designed to work across specialized hardware accelerators (chips optimized for AI) from different vendors.
contributions: CARAML benchmark suite for comprehensive evaluation of ML workloads on diverse accelerators
Custom power measurement tool (jpwr) for accurate energy consumption metrics
Systematic performance and energy characterization across NVIDIA, AMD, and Graphcore platforms
Extensible and reproducible benchmarking framework design

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: power consumption and energy efficiency during training

primary_theme: ML accelerator benchmarking and power evaluation
